absent: Software population-count implementation behind the architecture delegation and its handling of widths beyond the declared argument size.
Ordering, atomicity and failure semantics of the raw atomic long primitives referenced by atomic bit operations.
Behavior and side effects of race-detector instrumentation and barrier helpers invoked by instrumented wrappers.
Concrete value of machine word width and related constants on any specific build, and selection rule between alternative definitions for the same symbol.
Contents and construction of the byte reversal table used by the narrowest reversal helper.
Node representation, tree balancing, lookup insertion deletion algorithms, concurrency control and memory management of the associative array beyond its header and callback signatures.
Required bitmap length and result when no bit is set for the scheduler first-bit helper, and behavior of raw lowest and highest index helpers on zero input.
Locking protocol that ordered bit operations participate in and required pairing of acquire and release forms.
Exact configuration meaning of assuming plain writes atomic and its effect on observable races.

findings.text: Provides width-specific bit reversal helpers for eight, sixteen and thirty-two bit values. The narrowest form consults a table indexed by the input value, while wider forms combine two narrower reversals placed into high and low halves. All are pure inline helpers without effects beyond their argument.

Provides architecture population-count entry points for eight, sixteen, thirty-two and sixty-four bit inputs that forward to the corresponding software population-count implementation and return the number of set bits.

Defines compile-time population-count evaluation by summing per-bit presence for the low eight positions and composing wider widths from narrower halves. Public sized helpers select the compile-time form when the argument is a compile-time constant and the architecture form otherwise, while uppercase variants require a constant argument and the generic uppercase form widens through sixty-four bits.
Bit number decomposition for arrays of machine words: word index is the number divided by bits per word and mask is a single one shifted by the number modulo bits per word.
Provides atomic modify operations that affect one numbered bit inside an array of words. Each targets the word containing the requested number and applies set, clear or toggle semantics atomically.
Provides atomic read-modify-write operations that set, clear or toggle one numbered bit and report whether that bit was set before the update. The update applies to the containing word only.

Provides helpers to locate set bits and to rank the highest set bit. One helper reports the index of the lowest set bit in a word, another reports the index of the highest set bit, two sized helpers report one-based positions with zero meaning no bit set, a sixty-four bit helper extends that ranking across both halves with defined zero handling, and a complement helper locates the first zero bit.

Defines non-atomic modify operations on numbered bits that update the containing word with ordinary loads and stores. Variants set, clear, toggle, or combine the update with reporting the prior state of the bit. They provide no mutual exclusion and require external protection when shared.

Defines bit observation helpers that extract one bit from the containing word by shifting. The plain observer is documented as atomic and preserves volatile access to the underlying word, the acquire observer adds acquire ordering to the load, and a constant-oriented observer reads through a const view and normalizes the result to boolean.

Defines alias layers that unify naming across configuration choices. Constant-prefixed non-atomic names resolve to the generic non-atomic implementations, architecture triple-underscore and test names resolve to the generic forms, non-instrumented triple-underscore and test names resolve to architecture forms, and short public macro names dispatch through a common bit operation selector to the corresponding internal helper.

Provides public atomic bit operations that add race-detector instrumentation for the affected word and, for read-modify-write forms, a full ordering barrier before delegating to the architecture atomic implementation. The set, clear and toggle forms return nothing while the test-and forms return the prior state.

Provides bit operations with lock ordering for use in locking paths. Clearing with unlock semantics performs a release update, a double-underscore clearing variant combines an unordered read and mask removal with a release store, acquiring test-and-set first inspects the current word and only performs an acquire update when the bit appears clear, and a release xor helper updates a word and reports the prior state of position seven.

Instrumented lock wrappers add release or read-write instrumentation around the ordered primitives. Unlock paths mark a release before the update, while the locking test-and-set path instruments the accessed word as a read-write atomic access.

Provides instrumented non-atomic bit operations that record plain or atomic accesses to the affected word before delegating to the architecture non-atomic implementation. Pure writers use write instrumentation, pure readers use atomic read instrumentation, and read-modify-write helpers use a shared helper that varies instrumentation when plain writes are assumed atomic.

Defines little-endian ordered bit operations by transforming the requested number with a swizzle value before delegating to the native operation. The swizzle is zero on little-endian builds and derived from word width on big-endian builds, preserving least-significant-bit-first numbering across host orders.
Provides filesystem-oriented atomic bit aliases that delegate to the little-endian test-and-set and test-and-clear operations.

Entry point that returns the index of the first set bit in a small fixed-size bitmap. It examines two words on sixty-four bit builds and four words on thirty-two bit builds, using the lowest-set-bit helper with appropriate offsets, and fails compilation on other word widths.
Associative array header holding a pointer to the root node and a count of leaves currently in the tree. Both fields are initialized to empty by the init helper.

Callback table that adapts the associative array to caller key and object types. It supplies chunk extractors for index keys and objects at a given tree level, a predicate for object equality, a discriminator reporting the bit position where an object and key differ or negative when equal, and a destructor for objects.
Key material is processed in chunks sized to the machine word width.

Several hazards follow from the contracts. Non-atomic updates race when the same word is accessed concurrently even for distinct bits. Zero input is defined for one-based ranking helpers but not for raw lowest and highest index helpers which rely on undefined scan behavior. Bit numbers must lie within the mapped array since only word division and masking guard the access, and atomicity of plain observation depends on preserving volatile access and word-aligned storage.
